title: How Does Your Phone Understand Your Voice? 🎙️
description: How does your phone turn spoken words into precise text and commands? Take an amazing journey inside voice recognition technology.

scenes.say: How does your phone instantly obey your commands, turning vibrating air into precise digital actions?

scenes.caption: The Microphone
scenes.say: The journey starts when the microphone catches your voice. A thin diaphragm vibrates as sound wave pressure changes in the air.
This instant mechanical vibration turns into analog electrical signals, carrying your unique voice frequencies.

scenes.caption: Analog to Digital Converter
scenes.say: Digital processors don't understand analog signals. That is why a converter steps in to translate electrical signals into pure numbers.

scenes.label: Sampling Rate
scenes.say: Your phone takes sixteen thousand samples of your voice every single second to guarantee high accuracy.

scenes.title: Audio Spectrum Analysis
scenes.say: Software splits the audio into tiny pieces, analyzing frequencies to pinpoint phonemes and letters accurately.
Did you know? Modern systems rely on artificial neural networks that mimic the human brain in distinguishing words.
In the past, systems looked for exact rule matches. Today, they predict probabilities based on context and full sentences.

scenes.caption: Cloud Computing
scenes.say: Some phones send these chopped-up data chunks over the internet to massive servers with huge natural language processing power.
Servers compare audio data with billions of stored patterns to extract words that perfectly match your speech.
Thanks to modern processing chips, many phones now run this process locally without needing an internet connection.

scenes.title: Executing The Command
scenes.say: Once your voice becomes written text, the smart assistant interprets your intent and executes the command instantly.
This tech requires blocking ambient noise and wind, using multiple microphones to separate your voice from background sounds.
These systems train on millions of hours of recordings to understand various dialects and diverse voice tones.
